chunks: And with this chain of narrators, it was said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

A time will come upon my Ummah when only the script/outline of the Quran will remain, and of Islam only its name will remain; they will be called by it while they are furthest from it. Their mosques will be populous, yet they are desolate from guidance. The jurists of that time are the worst of jurists under the shadow of the sky; from them emerged the fitnah (strife), and to them it will return.

key_terms.رَسْمُهُ: Script or outline (referring to the physical text without understanding)
key_terms.فُقَهَاءُ: Jurists or scholars of Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the jurists in the time of decline according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the Shia concern with the distinction between *shari'ah* (form) and *haqiqa* (essence), warning that mere ritualism without inner guidance leads to spiritual ruin. The description of jurists (*fuqaha*) as the source of *fitna* reflects the historical context of political and theological fragmentation, where scholarly authority was often co-opted by ruling powers. This serves as a critical reminder for the Shia community to seek authentic knowledge that preserves both the letter and spirit of the Quran.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4.  The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “A time will come on my Ummah  when  only  the  name  of  the  Holy  Quran  will remain. They will have only the title of Islam while they will be far away from it. Their mosques will be filled apparently but will be completely  deprived of guidance. Their jurists will  be  worst  under  this  sky  and  mischief  will  start  from them and return to them.
